stories.title: Liquid sidechain prepares restart after white hats return $270M of $320M taken
stories.summary: The Liquid Bitcoin sidechain paused on September 7 after purported "white hat" actors withdrew about $320 million in BTC. A day later, about $270 million came back, and the network is preparing to restart. Reporting does not say why the funds were taken or returned.
stories.whyItMatters: A pause and partial recovery this large tests confidence in Bitcoin sidechain custody models.
whatToWatch: Confirmation the network has restarted
An accounting of the roughly $50M gap between taken and returned funds
Any official post-incident report from Liquid operators
questions: Who withdrew the funds, and why?
Will the remaining funds be returned?

stories.title: Tether-backed exchange freezes withdrawals after $7M leaves custody
stories.summary: A crypto exchange backed by Tether froze customer withdrawals after about $7 million left its custody, CryptoSlate reported. The exchange's name and the cause of the loss are not detailed in current reporting.
stories.whyItMatters: Tether sits at the center of crypto liquidity, so any custody failure at a linked exchange draws regulatory and market attention.
whatToWatch: An official statement from the exchange
Any comment from Tether
Whether withdrawals resume
questions: Which exchange is affected?
Was this a hack, an insider issue, or something else?

stories.title: Seven-year-old blockchain to shut down its own network and move to Ethereum
stories.summary: A blockchain that has run independently for seven years is abandoning its own network and migrating to Ethereum, per CryptoSlate. The supplied report does not name the chain or give a migration timeline.
stories.whyItMatters: Another independent chain folding into Ethereum points to ongoing consolidation among smaller layer-1 networks.
whatToWatch: The migration timeline and mechanics
What happens to existing holders and assets on the old chain
questions: Which blockchain is this?
Why abandon the network now?

stories.title: Ethereum Foundation names two 'must ship' EIPs for the Hegotá upgrade
stories.summary: The Ethereum Foundation has flagged two EIPs as "must ship" for the upcoming Hegotá network upgrade, Cointelegraph reported. The report does not identify the EIPs or give a firm upgrade date.
stories.whyItMatters: Naming must-ship EIPs signals which technical changes are locked in for Ethereum's next hard fork, which matters to developers and infrastructure operators.
whatToWatch: Confirmation of which two EIPs are involved
A firm date for the Hegotá upgrade
Testnet activation before mainnet
questions: Which two EIPs were named?
When is Hegotá expected to ship?

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation names 2 ‘must ship’ EIPs for Hegotá upgrade

stories.title: Vitalik Buterin says he is now confident AI won't break crypto
stories.summary: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said he is now confident that AI will not undermine crypto's core assumptions, and reportedly has staked a large share of his personal wealth on that view, per CryptoSlate. The report does not explain the form this "bet" takes.
stories.whyItMatters: Buterin's views carry weight in the Ethereum community, but a personal statement of confidence is not a technical guarantee against AI-related risks.
whatToWatch: Any concrete detail on what the stated bet actually involves
Further comment from Buterin on specific AI risks
questions: What does "betting 90% of his net worth" actually mean in practice?
What specific AI threat was he responding to?

sources.title: Vitalik Buterin now confident AI won’t break crypto, betting 90% of his net worth

stories.title: Harmony cites AI threats in proposal to shut down its blockchain
stories.summary: Harmony has proposed shutting down its blockchain and cited AI-related threats as a reason, according to Decrypt. The report does not detail the specific threats or the shutdown process.
stories.whyItMatters: A live layer-1 citing AI-specific security threats as grounds for shutdown would be an unusual and significant precedent.
whatToWatch: Whether the shutdown proposal moves to a formal vote
Disclosure of the specific AI threat cited
What happens to existing tokens and validators on Harmony
questions: What specific AI threat is being cited?
Is this proposal binding or just a discussion draft?

sources.title: Harmony Cites AI Threats in Proposed Blockchain Shutdown

stories.title: Yen intervention and US inflation data top this week's Bitcoin watch list
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's weekly Bitcoin outlook flags possible yen intervention by Japanese authorities and upcoming US inflation data as the main macro catalysts to watch this week. The piece is a roundup, not a single news event, so detail beyond these two threads is limited.
stories.whyItMatters: Currency intervention and US inflation prints are among the macro triggers most closely tied to short-term bitcoin price swings.
whatToWatch: This week's US inflation data release
Any confirmed yen intervention by Japan's central bank or finance ministry
Bitcoin's price reaction to both

stories.title: Australia removed 45 crypto and remittance registrations over the past year
stories.summary: An Australian regulator removed 45 crypto and remittance service registrations over the past year, Cointelegraph reported. The report does not name the regulator or give reasons for individual removals.
stories.whyItMatters: Registration removals are a concrete sign of tightening oversight on crypto and remittance providers in Australia.
whatToWatch: Further enforcement actions from the regulator
Any published list naming the removed entities
questions: Which regulator carried out the removals?
What triggered them: compliance failures, fraud, or inactivity?

stories.title: Capital B buys 376 more Bitcoin, lifting holdings to 3,521 BTC
stories.summary: Capital B purchased 376 additional bitcoin for about $29 million, bringing its total holdings to 3,521 BTC, Cointelegraph reported.
stories.whyItMatters: Continued corporate treasury buying is one data point on institutional bitcoin demand, though a single company's purchase should not be read as a broad market signal.
whatToWatch: Capital B's next disclosed purchase or holdings update
Other treasury companies' bitcoin buying activity
questions: How is the purchase being financed?
What is Capital B's average cost basis now?

stories.title: Brazilian banks expand crypto offerings as regulation takes hold
stories.summary: Banks in Brazil are expanding their crypto product offerings as the country's digital-asset regulatory framework takes hold, Decrypt reported. The report does not name specific banks or products.
stories.whyItMatters: Bank-level crypto adoption in a major Latin American market suggests regulatory clarity is opening mainstream access beyond crypto-native platforms.
whatToWatch: Which banks launch new crypto products
Further guidance from Brazilian regulators
Early adoption numbers
questions: Which banks and products are involved?
What does the regulatory framework require of participating banks?

stories.title: Liquid hackers return $270M of the $320M taken from the Bitcoin sidechain
stories.summary: Hackers who took about $320 million in bitcoin from the Liquid sidechain have returned roughly $270 million, Decrypt reported. Reporting does not identify those responsible or explain why most, but not all, funds were returned.
stories.whyItMatters: A recovery of this scale after a sidechain-level breach directly affects confidence in Bitcoin layer-2 and sidechain custody models.
whatToWatch: A full accounting of returned versus missing funds
Any statement from Blockstream or Liquid operators
The network's restart
questions: Who carried out the withdrawal?
Why was most, but not all, of the money returned?

sources.title: Liquid Hackers Return $270M in Bitcoin After Swiping $320 Million

stories.title: Solana beats Bitcoin on one metric, but a single bug could still take down the network
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Solana now outperforms Bitcoin on one unspecified metric, while cautioning that a single software bug could still bring down the Solana network. The report does not specify which metric or which bug is being referenced.
stories.whyItMatters: The report points to a persistent trade-off in Solana's design: strong performance against concentrated technical risk from its architecture.
whatToWatch: Any progress on client diversification for Solana
Network outages or incidents tied to the cited bug risk
questions: Which metric is Solana beating Bitcoin on?
What specific bug is being referenced, and has it been patched?

sources.title: Solana beats Bitcoin on one key metric, but a single software bug could still take down the network
